name: Question 12
problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{x}^{3}+{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}}
$$
worked_solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{x}^{3}+{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{3}+(vx)^{3}}{x(vx)^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{3}(1+{v}^{3})}{{v}^{2}{x}^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{1+{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{1}{{v}^{2}}+v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{{v}^{2}} \\ {v}^{2}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {v}^{2}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {v}^{2}\,\text{d}v & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{v}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}v & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{3} & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+3{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{3} & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we have let $C=3{C}_{1}.$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}\,.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{y}{x})}^{3} & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\ \frac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\ {y}^{3} & ={x}^{3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C) \\ y & =x\sqrt[3]{3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12

Use the transformation y=v(x)x to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

dydx=x3+y3xy2

a
y=x3ln⁡|x|+C3
b
 y=x2(3ln⁡|x|+C)
c
 y=x(3ln⁡|x|+C)
d
 y=xln⁡|x|+C
e
 y=x(2ln⁡|x|+C)2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

With y=v(x)x, we have dydx=xdvdx+vddx(x)=xdvdx+v.

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

dydx=x3+y3xy2xdvdx+v=x3+(vx)3x(vx)2xdvdx+v=x3(1+v3)v2x3xdvdx+v=1+v3v2xdvdx+v=1v2+vxdvdx=1v2v2dvdx=1x.

Integrating both sides with respect to x, we obtain ∫v2dvdxdx=∫1xdx∫v2dv=∫1xdxv33dv=ln⁡|x|+C1v3=3ln⁡|x|+3C1v3=3ln⁡|x|+C.

Note that we have let C=3C1.

From the transformation y=vx, we get v=yx. Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

(yx)3=3ln⁡|x|+Cy3x3=3ln⁡|x|+Cy3=x3(3ln⁡|x|+C)y=x3ln⁡|x|+C3.
